newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen recovering.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen recovering.

text.p: Gold prices in the Indian sub-continent are likely to gain in the next few days because of a firm trend in the world market, aided by fresh wedding season demand, dealers said on Monday.
A Bombay bullion dealer said the cost of imported gold was higher than domestic prices, making it a disincentive for Indian expatriates to bring in the metal.
Indian expatriates are allowed to bring in up to 10 kg of gold once every six months, subject to a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grammes.
Bombay bullion dealers said importers of gold paid nearly 800 rupees by way of costs and taxes on every 10 grammes.
"In fact imported gold today costs around 4,900 rupees per 10 grammes, including a 13.5 percent premium paid to acquire a special licence to import gold," said a bullion dealer.
"That's why imports are very poor and domestic prices very firm," he said.
The dealer said expatriates who did not need special licences also incurred expenditure to raise foreign exchange and to bring in gold.
"This is the simple arithmetics of cost plus expenses, which sometimes leaves hardly any margin," he said.
In the week to Monday, the price of standard gold 24 carats rose 75 rupees to 4,870 on the Bombay bullion market.
In Pakistan's main commercial city of Karachi, dealers said they would expect gold prices to move in a narrow range if the rupee stayed steady this week.
Noureen Hamid, marketing manager of ARY Traders, one of the largest gold importers in Pakistan, said gold prices would not change much unless the rupee was devalued.

Forex dealers said there was no sign of an imminent devaluation, with plentiful dollar inflows from abroad following Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's appeal to overseas Pakistanis to remit at least $1,000 each to increase foreign reserves.
One bullion dealer said gold demand had not risen much despite the current wedding season.
Dealers in Dubai, the re-export market for gold, said prices were upbeat, fanned by strong Indian wedding demand and buying ahead of a state-sponsored shopping festival in the Gulf emirate.
"Gold demand in Dubai is now pretty high...There is a shortage of physical gold in the market," said one trader.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $=35.88 Indian rupees 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams) * Bombay prices February 24/17, Karachi and Dubai February 23/1
